annotation_provenance: Authored in a single session, as NEW held-out material for Milestone 11-B's structured-representation design -- none of these sentences are drawn from or restate evaluation/m11/corpus.json (Milestone 11's own corpus), which this document uses only as qualitative DEVELOPMENT background, never re-described as newly held-out. Every field below was decided from first principles (what the SENTENCE actually means, independent of what today's production parser does with it) -- this milestone implements no code, so there is no 'current baseline outcome' to capture live the way M10E/M11-A1/M11-A2 did; the 'today' column in the design doc's own worked-example table is instead derived by direct inspection of the existing, unmodified parser/matcher contracts (JobRequirement's non-nullable necessity field, the concept registry, GithubObservability's three values), not by executing anything.

schema_notes.qualification_kind: SPECIFIC_TECHNOLOGY | TECHNICAL_COMPETENCY | EDUCATION | EXPERIENCE | NONTECHNICAL | OTHER_LEGITIMATE | UNINTERPRETABLE
schema_notes.necessity: REQUIRED | PREFERRED | null (genuinely unknown/unresolved -- NEVER a third enum member)
schema_notes.applicability_condition: null (unconditional) or the exact conditional clause, verbatim -- a SEPARATE dimension from necessity, never folded into it
schema_notes.interpretation_certainty: HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW -- reuses the EXISTING gitscore.jobs.types.ParserConfidence enum unchanged; LOW here means 'confident WHAT KIND of statement this is, but uncertain about one of its OTHER dimensions' (necessity/logical_composition/applicability) -- distinct from qualification_kind=UNINTERPRETABLE, which means 'not confident what kind of statement this even is'
schema_notes.normalized_reference: {type: 'concept', id: '<registry concept_id>'} | {type: 'competency_tag', id: '<free, unregistered slug>'} | null
schema_notes.github_observability: reuses the EXISTING gitscore.jobs.types.GithubObservability enum unchanged (NOT_OBSERVABLE | PARTIALLY_OBSERVABLE | STRONGLY_OBSERVABLE)
schema_notes.evidence_requirements: free-text, documentary only, never consumed by the matcher -- what WOULD plausibly count as evidence, if anything

controls.text: Experience with Rust is required.
controls.evidence_requirements: Repositories with substantive Rust source files, not a single trivial script.

controls.text: Deep understanding of concurrency and lock-free data structures is required.
controls.evidence_requirements: Implementations of lock-free/concurrent data structures, benchmark/profiling tooling, commit messages referencing race conditions -- fundamentally NOT a dependency-manifest scan.

controls.text: Strong foundation in circuit theory and power electronics is required.
controls.evidence_requirements: None plausible -- a hardware-design domain, not a software artifact, regardless of specificity.

controls.text: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
controls.evidence_requirements: None -- enrollment/degree status has no repository-level analogue.

controls.text: 5+ years of professional software engineering experience.
controls.evidence_requirements: None directly -- commit history TIMESPAN is a weak, never-asserted proxy; professional (paid) status is not GitHub-visible at all.

controls.text: Shipped at least one production web application.
controls.evidence_requirements: A deployed, non-trivial repository (CI/CD config, a live-looking app structure) is a genuine, if imperfect, proxy -- unlike years-of-experience, this phrasing names an ARTIFACT a repository could plausibly show.

controls.text: Strong written and verbal communication skills.
controls.evidence_requirements: None defensible -- README/PR-description quality is at most a weak, never-asserted proxy.

controls.text: Must be eligible to work in Canada.
controls.evidence_requirements: None -- legal work-authorization status is never GitHub-visible.

controls.text: Bachelor's degree required, unless you can demonstrate equivalent practical experience.
controls.applicability_condition: unless you can demonstrate equivalent practical experience
controls.evidence_requirements: None for the degree itself; the SUBSTITUTE ('equivalent practical experience') is a separate, EXPERIENCE-kind qualification this one sentence also implies but does not fully spell out -- flagged, not resolved, by this milestone (see doc Phase 4).

controls.text: Must obtain a government security clearance if the role requires it.
controls.evidence_requirements: None -- and the condition itself ('if the role requires it') is self-referential enough that even the EMPLOYER's own intent is underdetermined from the text alone, hence LOW rather than MEDIUM certainty.

controls.text: 5+ years of professional Go experience is required for this role, however, we are also open to exceptional entry-level candidates with strong fundamentals.
controls.applicability_condition: unless the candidate is an 'exceptional entry-level candidate with strong fundamentals' (the posting's own self-contradiction, not resolved by this representation -- see doc Phase 4)
controls.evidence_requirements: None -- LOW certainty is the model's own honest signal that a human reader, not an automated consumer, should see this exact caveat rather than a silently-picked REQUIRED/PREFERRED answer.

controls.text: Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
controls.evidence_requirements: PyTorch, TensorFlow, OR (per the illustrative 'such as') a plausible THIRD framework (JAX, Keras) the sentence never names -- today's schema has no field for 'exhaustive: false' at all (see doc Phase 2's old-to-new mapping); ParserConfidence.LOW is the closest EXISTING signal, but does not by itself tell a matcher to credit an unlisted framework.

controls.text: Proficiency in one of the following: Python, Java, or Go.
controls.evidence_requirements: Any one of the three languages, substantively -- the complete member list, confirmed by 'one of the following' (an exhaustive-list idiom, contrast m11b-illustrative-01's 'such as').

controls.text: Experience with CI/CD tooling (e.g., GitHub Actions, CircleCI) and observability tooling such as Prometheus or Datadog.
controls.evidence_requirements: An AND of two illustrative OR-groups (CI/CD tool X) AND (observability tool Y) -- today's flat `alternative_concept_ids` tuple cannot represent this at all; M10D's own Root Cause 6, still unaddressed. MIXED_UNSUPPORTED is this model's HONEST diagnostic value for exactly this shape -- never silently flattened into one over-permissive group, and never silently dropped either.

controls.text: 3+ years of professional experience building backend services in Python is required.
controls.evidence_requirements: Substantive Python backend-service repositories.

sibling_qualifications.note: the SAME sentence's experience-years claim -- already Milestone 6A's own documented precedent (JobRequirement docstring Part 1): ONE sentence, TWO independent qualification objects, never collapsed into one.

controls.text: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering and 2+ years of PCB design experience.
controls.evidence_requirements: None.

sibling_qualifications.note: the PCB-design-experience half of the same sentence.

controls.text: Applicants must know Java.
controls.evidence_requirements: Substantive Java repositories. Genuinely unsectioned -- qualification_kind/necessity are both fully determinable from the LOCAL sentence alone, independent of section-origin (M10E's own existing precedent: an explicit local marker always wins).

controls.text: The right candidate is comfortable learning new tools independently.
controls.evidence_requirements: None defensible. An applicant-side LEARNING-APTITUDE trait (M10E/M11's own 'Category C' distinction) -- never confused with a LEARNING-opportunity narrative despite sharing the word 'learning'; MEDIUM rather than HIGH certainty because 'the right candidate is' is a softer framing than an explicit 'required'/'must'.

controls.text: A strong technical background.
controls.evidence_requirements: None -- genuinely unclear whether this means SPECIFIC_TECHNOLOGY, TECHNICAL_COMPETENCY, or EXPERIENCE; UNINTERPRETABLE is the model's own honest answer to 'what KIND of statement is this,' distinct from a LOW-certainty-but-otherwise-typed claim.

controls.text: Contributions to a well-known open-source project are a plus.
controls.evidence_requirements: Cross-repository commit/PR history, especially to a recognizable project -- the SHARPEST contrast case in this corpus: a qualification with NO technology concept to normalize against at all, yet the single MOST directly GitHub-native claim possible. Confirms qualification_kind and github_observability are genuinely independent axes in BOTH directions (see also m11b-competency-02, the opposite extreme).

controls.text: Proven ability to profile and optimize CPU- and cache-bound code paths.
controls.evidence_requirements: Profiling scripts, benchmark suites, perf-sensitive commit history -- MEDIUM certainty because 'proven ability' could also be read as an EXPERIENCE-style claim (a track record) rather than a pure competency; this model does not force a single resolution, it records the uncertainty.
